_note: one entry for each placeholder @@...@@ of the post, keyed by its exact words: value, unit, a text for the page, and how it was computed. Losses are held-out losses in nats per token at the end of training. One seed a run unless an entry says two. Seed noise: twice the largest difference between two seeds of one rung of the ladder (100M tokens), 0.012 nats today; the swaps are single runs at 50M tokens, where no pair of seeds was run, so the threshold is borrowed from the ladder. Numbers are rounded to six significant digits first, as in the files the figures read.

results_lines.line 132: say whether the post-norm prof: No. At initialization post-norm is level, not rising: under GPT-2's initialization every block but the first receives the same gradient (0.079 at 48 blocks; the first, which reads the raw embedding, 0.94), and with Glorot weights the two ends differ by at most 23% and in no steady direction (1.35 to 1.58 at 12 blocks, 1.41 to 1.53 at 24 blocks, 1.99 to 1.53 at 48 blocks). Pre-norm is the one with a slope, and it falls toward the output: 3.59 to 1.25 at 48 blocks under GPT-2's initialization, 1.31 to 0.27 with Glorot weights, as its stream grows (1.14 to 6.62). The top-layer gradient with depth agrees with Proposition 5.2.5 in its own setting (Glorot weights): from 12 to 48 blocks it changes by a factor 0.94 for post-norm and 0.47 for pre-norm (1/sqrt(4) = 0.50); under GPT-2's initialization, whose 1/sqrt(2L) makes the pre-norm stream end at the same size at every depth (0.088, 0.088, 0.088), it does not change in either (1.00, 1.01). Training at 8 layers (the 2019 recipe, rate 0.0024, 50M tokens, one seed each): post-norm does not train with or without warmup (7.690, 7.690; for scale, token frequencies alone give 7.70 on held-out text (the unigram level of part 8's replayed run) and a uniform guess over the 32,768 tokens 10.40); pre-norm is not indifferent to warmup: 4.613 with, 5.706 without (1.09 behind). In the 2026 recipe (Muon, writers at zero, 50M tokens) post-norm does train: 4.133 against 4.026 for the same layer norm placed before the sublayers.
results_lines.line 150: say whether layer norm, RMS no: Layer norm (4.026) and RMS norm with a gain (4.025) are within 0.001 of each other; the parameter-free RMS norm of the recipe (4.045) is 0.020 behind them, more than seed noise (0.012): at this size the learned gain helps and centering does not matter. On the ladder the same step (rung 3, layer norm with gain to parameter-free RMS norm) cost +0.024. Dynamic tanh lands at 4.077, +0.031. Without normalization the model does not train even with zero-initialized projections: the loss was 5.98 at step 70 and not finite at step 80. One seed each.
results_lines.line 206: rank the six activations, say: Best to worst: SwiGLU 4.037, GeGLU 4.043, squared ReLU 4.045, GELU 4.046, SiLU 4.052, ReLU 4.063. Seed noise is 0.012: only ReLU (+0.018 against squared ReLU) is outside it; SwiGLU (−0.008), GeGLU (−0.002), GELU (+0.001) and SiLU (+0.007) are inside. The second-order units average 4.042 and the first-order ones 4.054: 0.012 apart, at the edge of noise and mostly ReLU's doing; GELU ties squared ReLU. The 0.02 to 0.05 of the literature is not there at 8 layers and 50M tokens: close to a null result. What does differ is what the units do: 83% of squared ReLU's activations and 86% of ReLU's are exact zeros, GELU has 1%; the kurtosis of the activations is 1306 for squared ReLU, 289 and 306 for the two gated units and 43 for GELU; dead units are rare in all six: none in 5 of them and 0.03% of the units at most (relu2).
results_lines.line 301: say whether the triggers of th: In part. The share of a neuron's 25 strongest triggers that end in its commonest last token is highest in block 2 (0.41) and lowest in block 12 (0.26); random positions give 0.08. Lower layers are the more shallow, as in the 2021 table, but by a modest margin. The top token of a value is the token after its key's strongest trigger for 1% of the neurons of block 1, 13% in block 9 and 5% in block 12 (chance 0.003%): values continue their triggers in the upper half, not at the very top. Coefficients are non-negative (squared ReLU). 200 neurons sampled a block, the 25 strongest triggers of each.
results_lines.line 353: say whether the three initiali: Only two of the three were run. With the writers scaled by 1/sqrt(2L) the 2026 recipe ends at 4.0438, with the writers at zero at 4.0451: 0.0013 apart, inside seed noise. During training the two cross: −0.010 at 10M tokens, +0.010 at 20M tokens (scaled less zero). No difference at the end and none that lasts early, at 8 layers. Plain 0.02 on every matrix was not run, so the sources' claim that the scaled rule clearly beats it is untested here. On the ladder, under AdamW at 100M tokens, zero writers were −0.026 against the scaled rule (rung 6 has 1 seed).
results_lines.line 447: name the two or three swaps th: Swapped back into the 2026 recipe, the rows of the table that cost the most: learned positions +0.112, no query-key normalization +0.029; among the other swaps, worse by more than noise: pos-none +0.264, pos-sinusoidal +0.133, norm-post +0.088, attn-mqa +0.050, norm-dyt +0.031, sched-cosine +0.031, attn-gqa2 +0.030, act-relu +0.018, no-embed-norm +0.014, and without normalization the run diverged. Inside seed noise (0.012): act-swiglu −0.008, no-softcap −0.002, act-geglu −0.002, init-gpt2 −0.001, tied 0.000, act-gelu +0.001, attn-qk-learned +0.001, pos-alibi +0.002, attn-gqa4 +0.003, act-silu +0.007. The other way, the old part better by more than noise: bias −0.021, norm-rmsnorm-gain −0.020, norm-layernorm −0.019. The full 2019 recipe ends at 4.144 and the full 2026 recipe at 3.814 (the ladder, 100M tokens): a gap of 0.330, of which the optimizer (rung 7) is 0.156 (47%) and the eight changes to the block 0.173 (53%); rotary positions alone are 0.110. Rung by rung: no-biases −0.009, rotary −0.110, rmsnorm +0.024, relu2 −0.025, qk-norm −0.011, zero-init −0.026, muon −0.156, untied −0.011, softcap −0.003. At 8 layers and 50M tokens three parts of the 2026 block are not better than what they replaced: with a learned gain the norm is 0.020 better (layer norm 0.019), with biases the model is 0.021 better, and GELU ties squared ReLU (+0.001); one seed each, against a seed spread of up to 0.006. What is clearly worth something: rotary positions (+0.112 with a learned table), the optimizer (−0.156 on the ladder), query-key normalization (+0.029 without) and pre-norm (+0.088 with post-norm and layer norm, +0.107 against the same layer norm before the sublayers). The norm on the embedding is at the edge: +0.014 without it, 0.000 when it goes together with the second vocabulary matrix (the tied run, 16.8M parameters fewer). The ladder and the swaps ask different questions and twice give different answers: squared ReLU gained 0.025 on the ladder (under AdamW, right after the norm lost its gain) and GELU put back into the finished recipe costs +0.001; writers at zero gained 0.026 on the ladder and the scaled rule put back costs −0.001. Query-key normalization goes the other way: −0.011 on the ladder, +0.029 when taken out of the finished recipe.
